findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
FOLLOW UP REPEAT:
(i) The baffles of the hood system were previously coated with grease as to be observed with hanging debris. The operator has since the last inspection replaced 7 of 8 baffles with brand new baffles, with the 8th baffle to be replaced shortly.
(ii) There is dust and grease hanging from the Ansul system. See that the hood duct work is cleaned. The operator has scheduled hood maintenance for the end of May.
Inspector will Follow Up on 1 June 2026 to check that the hood has been cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Observed the following storage order issues:
(i) Eggs being stored over milk in the display coolers of the retail portion of the facility. Store the eggs beneath milk. Move the eggs away from the milk by Follow Up 21 May 2026.
(ii) Raw chicken stored over lettuce in the base of the prep cooler of the kitchen. CORRECTED ON SITE. Lettuce was moved during the inspection. 
See that foods are stored in-order of cooking temperatures to avoid cross contamination. Cease storing raw proteins over ready-to-eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: The baffles of the hood system are so coated with grease as to be observed with hanging debris. There is dust and grease hanging from the Ansul system and the baffles of the entire system. The last cleaning listed for the hood is CFB for 2024. Operator was unable to indicate when the last time the hood was cleaned. See that the hood duct work is cleaned. Clean the baffles. Inspector will Follow Up on 21 May 2026 to check that the hood has been cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the slushie machine nozzles to have soiled debris. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and cleaned them during the inspection. Ensure that equipment food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that there was no sanitizer bucket in the facility. CORRECTED: PIC was informed, and with inspectors made a sanitizer bucket using bleach (Chlorine) which tested at effective concentrations. Ensure that an effective chemical sanitizer solution is available for cleaning at all times.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
findings.comment: Observed metal bowls used to toss cooked fried food with RTE sauces and seasonings. When asked how often they are cleaned, the PIC stated every night. Inspectors informed the PIC that in-use saucing bowls should be cleaned every 4 hours. CORRECTED: the bowls were cleaned, and the PIC and inspectors created a formal TIME AS CONTROL STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE for the saucing bowls: “Remove all saucing bowls for cleaning [Wash, Rinse, Sanitize, Air Dry] at the following times: 3:00PM, 7:00PM, and CLOSING TIME”. Ensure that food that is not kept under temperature control is instead kept under time control.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(5) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (5) The FOOD in unmarked containers or PACKAGES, or marked to exceed a 4-hour limit shall be discarded.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed disinfecting wipes stored with food and single-use/single-service articles and utensils. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and the items were moved to a separate area away from food and single-use/single-service articles and utensils. Ensure that toxic materials like cleaning chemicals are stored so they CANNOT contaminate food and single-use/single-service articles and utensils.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Observed fish thawing in a sink of water without running water. Faucet was turned on twice before staff was appropriately conveyed knowledge of proper thawing. Discussed thawing being a process significantly different from a process we complete in our homes. Triple sinks were designed to allow for water to overflow. PIC also recognized that thawing the fish in a cooler was an approved thawing method. CORRECTED: through education and practice. Ensure that proteins are thawed using a method that does not allow thawed portions of RTE food to rise above 5°C (41°F).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed a clean cutting board being stored behind the faucet of the double sink. This storage practice should cease as it allows for splash from the ‘mop’ sink to come into contact with the board. CORRECTED through storage: during the inspection, the cutting board was properly stored on a storage shelf away from the splash of the sink. Ensure equipment and utensils are stored where they are not exposed to contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Observed a rubber spatula to be damaged to the point where 50% of the face was ripped away. CORRECTED: PIC discarded the spatula during the inspection. Cease using materials once they have become damaged or broken.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the facility to be using cardboard to hold portion cups of sauces. Cease use of cardboard and use materials that are smooth and easily cleanable. Most of the facility storage containers are plastic. Follow suit and replace cardboard containers with similar plastic containers.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the reach-in freezers in the extra storage room to have a soiled lid AND observed the base shelf beneath the wooded grates of the kitchen 4 door cooler (beneath chicken boxes) to be soiled. Clean these cold storage units by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: Observed mop water to be grey and cold in the mop bucket. The mop bucket was moved from in-front of the hand sink (not obstructing) to the back room without being emptied. See that mop water is emptied after use and not allowed to remain stagnant in the bucket. CORRECTED: PIC emptied the mop bucket during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: Observed that the grease trap has a strong sewer oder emanating from the unit and appears to have a flaking metal lid. Upon calling Ace Disposal (the company serviced the grease trap 19 March 2026), it appears the grease trap has a missing baffle, broken lid, and damaged container. The grease trap has failed. The repair will be costly and SCDPH is giving six (6) month to complete this task (12 November 2026). Keep SCDPH updated on repair progress until then.
findings.citation_text: 5-403.11 Approved Sewage Disposal System. SEWAGE shall be disposed through an APPROVED facility that is: (A) A public SEWAGE treatment plant; or (B) An individual SEWAGE disposal system that is sized, constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed that personal items, including clothing and personal food, are being stored next to food and single-use/single-service articles and utensils. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and the items were moved to a separate area. Ensure that suitable facilities are used for the orderly storage of employee clothing and other possessions.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The two employees working at the time of inspection could not produce food manager certificates. The only employee who is food manager certified wasn't present during the visit. Ensure that there is at least two employees who are a certified food protection managers to cover all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There wasn’t any hand soap available at the kitchen’s handwashing sink. The soap dispenser’s bag appeared empty. A bottle of dawn dish soap was provided to the sink to correct the violation. Discussed purchasing hand-soap in the near future to replace the dish soap. Ensure that there is always hand-soap present at every hand-sink to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
There was improper storage order in the following prep coolers in the kitchen area:
- Two containers of raw chicken were stored above sliced cheeses and lettuce heads 
- A container of raw beef was observed directly above dressings and other sauces

Discussed with the person-in-charge and the raw meats were rearranged in a manner that protects against contamination of RTE (ready-to-eat) foods. Ensure that raw animal protein is always stored below RTE foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Two gallons of whole milk were observed to exceed the manufacturer’s use by date. The use by date was 12/13/2024. Discussed with PIC and milks were discarded. Ensure that milks never exceed the manufacturer’s use by day and are discarded if the expiration date is exceeded. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed a bowl of cooked chicken to be stored underneath a container of raw chicken in a cooler along the cook-line. Discussed with PIC and the bowl of cooked chicken was rearranged. Ensure that cooked food is always stored above raw meats to protect against cross contamination. 

3-305.12: FOOD may not be stored: (A) In locker rooms; (B) In toilet rooms; (C) In dressing rooms; (D) In garbage rooms; (E) In mechanical rooms; (F) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (G) Under leaking water lines, including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads, or under lines on which water has condensed; (H) Under open stairwells; or (I) Under other sources of contamination.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: The hand sink at the start of the inspection was observed to be blocked by various items. When this was noted to the PIC, all items in the hand sink were removed, thus resulting in the hand sink being accessible. Ensure the hand sink remains accessible during all hours of operation and is only used for hand washing. 
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: At the start of the inspection, the cutting boards were observed to be stored against the back portion of the double sink faucet which is a contamination hazard for the surfaces being stored on them and a potential contamination of hands touching the surface of the cutting boards when the sink is used. The PIC has moved these boards from this location to a more appropriate location to not pose a contamination hazard. The PIC will be finding a new place to store the cutting boards to air dry without posing a contaminants hazard. 
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: There was a knife observed stored between the magnetic knife strip and the wall. This knife was removed and placed into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. Ensure that knives are stored properly on the magnetic strip to prevent contamination of the food contact surface.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: At the start of the inspection, the sanitizer bucket was not made up and therefore tested at 0ppm. During the inspection, the sanitizer bucket was created and tested at 200ppm QUAT. Ensure that a sanitizer bucket is readily available during all hours of operation and tested to ensure proper concentrations.  
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. 
(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: There is observed an accumulation of food debris at the bottom of the reach in freezer. Ensure that this freezer is thoroughly cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean.  
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: At the dish area, it is observed that there are several anchors in the wall with visible holes in the wall. PIC was made aware of these holes. A solution of caulking placed into these holes has been discussed. Ensure materials and surfaces are smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable. 
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The cook line floor, especially under the fryers, is observed to have an excessive accumulation of grease and food debris. Ensure that the equipment is pulled away from the wall and that the floor and nearby walls are cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-303.11: The hood system was observed to only have one lightbulb currently working and three that are burnt out. Due to manufacturers specifications of 4 bulbs, all 4 bulbs need to be operating. Ensure the bulbs are replaced to allow appropriate lighting in this area. 
6-303.11: The light intensity shall be at least a certain lux and present in certain areas.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
No reporting agreements were signed by staff. Employee reporting agreements must be signed by all staff to ensure employees do not come to work sick. Employee reporting agreements were signed by staff during the inspection. Extra copies were given to the manager. 

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed an employee wash his hands and turn the faucet off without using a barrier. Ensure a barrier is used when operating faucet after hands are washed. Education provided during the inspection. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed no sanitizer bucket or solution made and available for use during the inspection. A sanitizer solution of bleach (100ppm) was made to correct the violation. Ensure a sanitizer solution is available to clean food contact surfaces during all hours of food preparation and operation. 

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
findings.comment:
Observed the grease dumpster to be overfilled. The grease was overflowing onto the parking lot behind the building. Ensure the grease dumpster is checked regularly and pumped regularly so the dumpster does not overfill. Ace Grease is going to service the grease dumpster on 10-5-22 so it does not remain overfilled. 

5-501.116: (A) Receptacles and waste handling units shall be cleaned in way to prevent contamination. (B) Receptacles and waste handling units shall be cleaned at frequency to prevent buildup.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed no shields on lights in the kitchen prep area and above the 3 part sink. Ensure the lights are shielded or shatter resistant.  

6-202.11: Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated or otherwise shatter-resistant in certain areas.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: Observed cheesecake in the cooler to be held at a temperature of 52 F inside the desert cooler. The manager stated the cooler was working earlier this morning and that the cooler was probably on a defrost cycle. Pudding in the bottom of the cooler was 42 F. The cooler was checked 20 minutes later and had dropped temperature. Discussed temperature logs with the PIC. 
(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: Observed tubs of chicken to not be date marked in the prep cooler and the four-door cooler. These tubs should be date marked with a 7 day date marking to ensure no old food is used. The manager stated the chicken was gotten a few days ago and he would dat mark the tubs to correct the violation. 

(A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf).

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: Observed coolers to not have thermometers inside the coolers to check the internal air temperature of the cooler. Thermometers must be put inside each cooler. 

(A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf
